race.name: Wyścig by Tomasz Marczyński — Niepołomice
race.tagline: Ninety-nine fast forest kilometres with just enough technical ground to punish lazy positioning.

vitals.registration: Online through September 18, 2026. Basic entry: 199 PLN
vitals.aid_stations: On-course buffet included with entry; exact locations not published
route_options: Long: 99 km and approximately 271 m climbing from the official GPX
Short: 47 km and approximately 131 m climbing from the official GPX

climate.description: The organizer does not publish a race-day temperature range. September in the Niepołomice Forest can be mild or wet, so the dependable preparation signal is variable traction rather than heat or altitude.
challenges: Rain can change fast forest tracks

terrain.surface: The official long-course GPX covers 99 km with approximately 271 m of accumulated climbing. The organizer describes lightning-fast gravel tracks mixed with technical forest segments and a signature hairpin in a clearing.

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The ninth edition has a real operating history, professional timing, a former WorldTour rider behind it, and a strong Kraków-area festival. The flat course and regional rather than international field keep it at 59 and Tier 3.

biased_opinion.summary: This is not a climbing contest. The long GPX gains only about 271 metres in 99 kilometres, so the race is decided by positioning, repeated accelerations, surface speed, and whether you can keep eating while the group refuses to settle down.
strengths: Festival and after-party tied to the Kraków cycling community
Fast course that rewards real race craft
weaknesses: No published field-size or cutoff figures
Limited evidence of international field depth
Organizer does not publish exact aid locations
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A legitimate regional Polish gravel race where flat does not mean easy; train speed durability and pack skills, not mountain climbing.

final_verdict.one_liner: A fast, established forest race that makes you earn every metre through speed rather than elevation.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want tactical, high-speed gravel near Kraków; skip it if your idea of gravel requires a mountain profile.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a longer Polish ultra-format, compare Sudovia Gravel.

logistics.airport: Kraków John Paul II International Airport; verify race-day transfers to Niepołomice
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Niepołomice for race-morning simplicity or Kraków for the organizer's end-of-season after-party
logistics.food: Entry includes a recovery meal and on-course buffet; carry race nutrition for a fast event where stopping costs the group
logistics.packet_pickup: Race-office details are governed by the organizer's current regulations
logistics.parking: Not published on the English event page

eligibility.status_note: The September 19, 2026 edition is open for registration with official long and short GPX files and published regulations.

history.origin_story: Niepołomice hosted the first Wyścig by Tomasz Marczyński and returns as the ninth-edition 2026 season finale.
notable_moments: The 2026 event adds the J-Labs Polish IT Industry Gravel Championships on the 47 km course
history.reputation: An established southern-Poland cycling event built around the Niepołomice Forest and Kraków cycling community.

course_description.character: A nearly flat 99 km forest race where sustained speed, group position, and repeated accelerations matter more than climbing watts.

suffering_zones.label: Opening Selection
suffering_zones.desc: The flat profile encourages an immediate high-speed race; losing the useful group is more expensive than any climb.

suffering_zones.label: Mid-Race Speed Debt
suffering_zones.desc: At halfway, repeated accelerations and vibration—not accumulated vertical gain—start separating riders who trained only steady endurance.

suffering_zones.label: The Clearing Hairpin
suffering_zones.desc: The organizer's signature hairpin rewards position and clean braking before the final run toward Niepołomice.
suffering_zones.terrain_detail: Technical turn on otherwise fast ground

course_description.signature_challenge: Holding race speed for 99 km on a course too flat to give you a recovery climb or a safe place to drift backward.

guide_variables.race_terrain: Fast forest gravel with short technical sectors
guide_variables.race_weather: Variable early-autumn conditions; exact organizer range not published

non_negotiables.why: The 99 km course has only about 271 m climbing, so speed durability defines the day.
Fast forest racing creates repeated accelerations without long recovery climbs.
A flat group race punishes riders who need to stop or sit up to eat.

migration_notes: Added the authoritative real Polish event after tombstoning the fabricated generic polish-gravel profile
Distance and elevation come from the organizer's 2026 GPX; accumulated positive elevation was computed from track points
No TrainingPeaks fleet was claimed at profile creation; pack remains pending

logistics.explanation: Niepołomice sits close enough to Kraków for international access, but the organizer has not published parking or transfer detail on the English event page.

length.explanation: The official long GPX is 99 km, placing it just over the rubric's 60-mile threshold.

technicality.explanation: The organizer describes technical forest segments and a signature hairpin, but the dominant character is fast gravel rather than extreme terrain.

elevation.explanation: The official 99 km GPX accumulates only about 271 m, or 889 feet, well below the 2,000-foot threshold.

climate.explanation: Early-autumn rain can alter forest traction, but there is no evidence of routinely extreme heat, cold, or storms.

altitude.explanation: The GPX stays roughly between 197 and 212 m above sea level, so altitude is irrelevant.

adventure.explanation: Racing through the Niepołomice Forest and finishing a long-running local series is memorable, though not remote expedition terrain.

prestige.explanation: Nine editions, Tomasz Marczyński's name, and a national industry championship create real Polish recognition without establishing international-icon status.

race_quality.explanation: Official GPX files, published regulations, professional Race Result registration, course buffet, and a full event festival indicate a professional regional operation.

experience.explanation: The forest race, castle expo, junior event, recovery meal, and Kraków after-party create more than a bare start-and-finish transaction.

community.explanation: The organizer explicitly ties the ninth edition to the Kraków cycling community and runs a multi-generational festival and season finale.

field_depth.explanation: The event is competitive and team-classified, but the organizer does not publish an entrant count or evidence of a deep international field.

value.explanation: 199 PLN includes timing, a start package, on-course buffet, and recovery meal, which is strong value for a fully operated event.

expenses.explanation: Regional Polish pricing and access from Kraków keep the likely trip below major destination-race costs for European riders.

topics.positioning: Staying in the useful group on flat gravel
topics.fueling: Eating and drinking at race speed
topics.surface_skill: Braking and cornering on fast forest tracks

marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: A nearly flat ninth-edition race where positioning and speed durability replace mountain climbing.
